generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential 1..N per table, no NULL, no duplicates; PK dedup runs after FK fill for tables whose PK is also an FK.
generic_sampling_rules.text_fk: Copy from parent key pool; allow NULL only where column is nullable; reserve at least one parent key from the pool so some parent rows have no children.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a small pool of realistic strings; allow near-variants and duplicates where DISTINCT is targeted.
generic_sampling_rules.text_year: Sample 4-digit year strings in 2000..2020; boundary values per exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.real_amount: Sample positive real with 2 decimals in 1.00..5000.00.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For every nullable column, ~10% NULL rows per instance, at least one NULL row; use the compact DB's measured share per column when available; planted NULLs are never replaced.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_values: 0.3 of text values drawn fresh from a small synthetic pool; rest reused to create duplicates.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_share: For DISTINCT-targeted columns, construct exactly ceil(0.2*n)..floor(0.5*n) duplicate values deterministically rather than probabilistically.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_distinct: Boundary samplers for year columns must allow at least 3 distinct values per instance so all listed boundary targets can appear.

issues.title: Generated foreign keys are not drawn from the parent key pools actually present
issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports 274 new FK violations across all 20 instances (purchase.Member_ID 76, purchase.Branch_ID 73, membership_register_branch.Member_ID 64, membership_register_branch.Branch_ID 61). In instance.py, `_make_sampler_for_column` returns an IntRangeSampler for member.Member_ID, membership_register_branch.Member_ID and purchase.Member_ID producing values 100..900 (distinct, sequential from start>max original). FK columns are then overwritten by `fill_foreign_keys_consistently`, whose pool comes from `_parent_key_pool` = `schema.original_values[(pt,pc)]` plus `instance[pt][pc]`. But `inst` is keyed per table only after the parent table was fully built, and member/branch generated PKs are 100..900 sequential values which are only appended if the writer inserted them. Writer uses `pragma foreign_keys = OFF` and never validates the appended child rows against generated parent keys; more critically, `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` is invoked before the child FK column is filtered by primary-key dedup / drop_unique_duplicates / row-count mismatch, so the actual inserted row count differs from n and position-indexed FK values no longer align. Regardless of mechanism, the observed 274 FK violations show the parent pool used for FK filling does not match the keys actually written.
issues.requested_revision: After building parent tables, capture exactly the PK values that will be written for each parent table (i.e. post-dedup), and use only that list as the FK pool. Respect the actual final row count n' after primary-key/dedup filtering when building FK columns. Verify by running `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` on each written instance; no new FK violations may be reported.

issues.title: Compact DB rows are not preserved (30 rows changed/missing per instance)
issues.evidence: Run report: every instance lists `dc_rows_missing_or_changed: 30` (member 180/20inst, branch 160/20inst, membership_register_branch 140/20inst, purchase 120/20inst). `write_instance_sqlite` copies the compact DB with `shutil.copyfile` when `orig_path` is given, but the CLI passes `orig_path` as None (`build_random_instance`, then `write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p)` with no orig_path). The writer then creates empty tables from `schema.ddl` and appends generated rows only — the compact rows are never present, which is exactly `compact_rows_missing` for 20/20. Also `cli._one` calls `write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p)` with no `orig_path`, and `_init` never stores the original path.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the compact DB path (`a['orig']`) through to `write_instance_sqlite` so the file copy happens, or have `instance.build_random_instance` also return the compact rows and merge them. After generation, verify compact rows are byte-identical (count and content) and no generated PK collides with a compact PK.

issues.title: instance.py aliasing `inst` to b in `_parent_key_pool` and self-referencing FK lookup
issues.evidence: `_parent_key_pool(schema, instance, table, pt, pc)` reads `instance.get(pt, {})` — but `pt` is the parent table; because tables are iterated in `schema.table_order` (parent-before-child levels), the parent key exists at that moment. However `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` is called with `inst` before `inst[t]` is set, and the returned `cols.update(fk_cols)` writes FK columns keyed by column name only (e.g. 'Member_ID'), overwriting the *Member_ID sampler* value on `membership_register_branch` and `purchase` — that is fine — but also on `member` (self-FK not present so no) and `branch`. On `member` the PK `Member_ID` is not a FK so kept. The real defect is that the parent pool `schema.original_values[(pt,pc)]` contains compact IDs that may not exist when the writer builds an empty DB (see issue 2), and `instance[pt][pc]` for a parent whose row-count was reduced by dedup includes values that never got written.
issues.requested_revision: Compute post-dedup parent PK lists once, store them on `inst[_final_pk]`, and have `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` consume those. Also ensure FK filling occurs after all parent dedup/drop steps.

issues.title: Group-size targets (1, 2, >=3) are not enforced by the samplers that own the groups
issues.evidence: Spec lists `branch.Branch_ID group_sizes: 1, 2 and >= 3`, `branch.Open_year group_sizes`, `branch.Name group_sizes`, `member.Level group_sizes`. `spec_samplers.sample_group_sizes` is defined but `instance._make_sampler_for_column` never calls it — instead it returns `IntRangeSampler(..., distinct=1)` for Branch_ID, `BoundaryTextSampler(..., max_distinct=6)` for Open_year, `TextPoolSampler` for Name, and `IntRangeSampler(..., max_distinct=3)` for Level. `max_distinct` clamps repeat sampling to a *previously drawn* value, which creates many-group of size 1 behaviour depending on luck, but does not enforce existence of groups of size 2 and >=3 in each instance. There is no post-sampling check that each target size occurs. Same for `member.Member_ID group_sizes` (minor_patterns).
issues.requested_revision: Use `sample_group_sizes` for the grouping columns (or assign labels via group-sizes helper then choose values per group), and validate for each instance that group sizes 1, 2 and >=3 occur for branch.Branch_ID, branch.Open_year, branch.Name, member.Level. Or drop those exceptions from the spec if the current 'random distinct draw' is accepted.

issues.title: Duplicate-share targets on Card_Number / member.Name not measured
issues.evidence: Spec requires 20-50% duplicate share on `member.Card_Number` and `member.Name`. `CardNumberSampler` sets dup_share=0.35 and `TextPoolSampler` for Name sets dup_share=0.35 — plausible but the samplers accept any pool, and `_make_sampler_for_column` passes `pool = schema.original_values.get((table, name), [])` which may be empty; when empty, `TextPoolSampler._fresh` produces unique-ish strings and duplicate share collapses. No instance-level validation of the measured duplicate share exists in execution feedback or in code.
issues.requested_revision: Assert per-instance duplicate share for these columns is within 20-50% after generation (or document that the sampler may fail). Provide fresh_pool seeded with repeating tokens so the target is achievable even with empty pool.

issues.title: NULL share for membership_register_branch.Branch_ID not derived from compact DB
issues.evidence: The spec says null share follows the compact DB share; `instance.build_random_instance` hard-codes `null_share=0.1` in `fill_foreign_keys_consistently`, and the spec explicitly states the target is 5-30%. The compact-database null share is not read here (schema.null_share exists, but is not consulted for FK branches). On this dataset the observed generated NULLs are 3/20 = 15%, within 5-30% but not derived from compact share; on other compact DBs with e.g. 0% NULLs, this would plant NULLs contradicting the 'follow compact share' rule.
issues.requested_revision: Read `schema.null_share[(table,col)]` for the FK column and clamp to 5-30% only when the spec explicitly overrides; otherwise follow the compact share (with at least one NULL when share > 0).

issues.title: membership_register_branch.Branch_ID PK / FK duplication risk
issues.evidence: membership_register_branch primary key is Member_ID; Branch_ID is FK to branch. `_make_sampler_for_column` returns None for Branch_ID and lets `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` draw from the parent pool. That is correct in intent, but `_make_sampler_for_column` returns an IntRangeSampler for `membership_register_branch.Member_ID` and then `sample_fresh_primary_keys` drops duplicates — which shortens the list; the FK columns Branch_ID drawn earlier remain at length n, so the Branch_ID list becomes misaligned with Member_ID after dedup. That directly produces new FK rows pointing at wrong Member_IDs and is a candidate cause of the observed FK violations.
issues.requested_revision: Recompute FK columns after PK dedup and unique-column drops, not before. Or restructure: build a row-tuple list first, filter invalid PK rows, then (re)assign FK values from the (final) parent pool.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 units fail with KeyError('Member_ID') at tscore_gen/instance.py:35 in _dedup_pk: `k = tuple(columns[c][i] for c in table_meta.primary_key)`. The program's _fill_fk_columns plants NULLs for nullable FK columns using schema.null_share, and _plant_nulls handles non-FK nullable columns. However, the spec's per_column_exceptions only lists membership_register_branch.Branch_ID for null_rows; other nullable columns (e.g., member.Hometown, branch.Address_road) are not explicitly covered. The program does plant NULLs for them via null_share, which is consistent with the interface rule, but the spec should state this.

issues.evidence: The spec requires group_sizes targets (1, 2, >=3) for branch.Branch_ID, branch.Open_year, branch.Name, member.Level. The program applies GroupedTextSampler/GroupedIntSampler/TextBoundarySampler to Name, Open_year, Level, but for branch.Branch_ID it uses IntRangeSampler with distinct=1 (sequential PKs), so group sizes on Branch_ID are always 1. The spec's per_column_exceptions lists group_sizes for branch.Branch_ID, which is unachievable with a unique PK.

issues.evidence: The spec requires purchase.Year boundary targets 2017,2018,2019 and Register_Year 2013-2017. This may prevent covering all boundary values in a single instance (only 2 distinct values per instance). The spec does not mandate max_distinct=2.

However, TextPoolSampler's _fresh() can produce values that collide with pool values, and the duplicate share is probabilistic, not guaranteed. With n=10, the realized duplicate share may fall outside 20-50%.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: every one of 20 instances is invalid with new_integrity_failures; 292 FK violations total (purchase.Member_ID 90, purchase.Branch_ID 78, membership_register_branch.Member_ID 77, membership_register_branch.Branch_ID 47). The writer disables FK enforcement (`con.execute('pragma foreign_keys = OFF')` in writer.py) and inserts generated rows whose FK values are not present in the parent tables.
issues.requested_revision: Fix FK generation so every generated child FK value exists in the parent table. The root cause is that `_fk_parent_pool` in instance.py builds the pool from `schema.original_values` (compact rows) plus `inst_pk`, but the generated parent PKs are produced by `IntRangeSampler` starting at `_compact_int_max+1` while the child FK filler draws from a pool that includes compact values and generated values — yet the writer inserts into a copy of the compact DB where the generated parent rows are also inserted, so the mismatch must be traced. Concretely: verify that the parent PK values actually written equal the values placed in `inst_pk` (the `_dedup_pk`/`_drop_unique_duplicates` filtering can shrink the parent column list after `inst_pk` is recorded, and `n_final` for the child may exceed the number of parent rows actually inserted). Ensure the FK pool is built from the exact final parent PK list that the writer inserts, and re-enable `pragma foreign_keys = ON` (or validate FK integrity before commit) so violations are caught rather than silently written.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: `membership_register_branch` rows_skipped = 78 across 20 instances (e.g. 113 added vs 78 skipped), and `purchase` skipped 1. The writer's fallback path rolls back and re-inserts row-by-row, counting failures as skipped. This means the intended table sizes (spec: membership_register_branch 8, purchase 8 per instance) are not met and the PK+FK sampling is producing rows that violate constraints.
issues.requested_revision: Diagnose why membership_register_branch rows are rejected. The PK+FK filler samples `Member_ID` without replacement from the parent pool, but the pool includes compact member IDs plus generated member IDs; if the generated member PKs are not actually inserted (or are deduped away), the FK fails. Also `Branch_ID` is nullable and planted with NULLs, but the PK is `Member_ID` only, so NULL Branch_ID should be allowed — confirm the rejection is the Member_ID FK, not a NOT NULL issue. Make the generator fail loudly (raise) instead of silently skipping rows when a generated row violates a constraint, so the spec's table sizes are guaranteed.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback nullable_columns: `membership_register_branch.Register_Year: generated rows: NULL 0 / 106` and `purchase.Total_pounds: generated rows: NULL 0 / 187`. The NULL rule requires every nullable column to have at least one NULL row per instance. In instance.py, `_plant_nulls` is only applied when `schema.null_share.get(key, 0.0) > 0`; if the compact DB has no NULLs in these columns, `null_share` is 0 and no NULLs are planted. The spec's `null_share` generic rule says '~10% NULL rows per instance, at least one NULL row' for every nullable column.
issues.requested_revision: In instance.py, for nullable non-FK columns, plant at least one NULL per instance even when the measured compact share is 0 (use `max(measured_share, 1/n)` or a floor of one NULL). The current code `if ns > 0: cols[cm.name] = _plant_nulls(...)` skips planting entirely when ns == 0.

issues.evidence: Specification `semantic_rules_and_formulas` for branch.Open_year says `CAST(Open_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2020` and marks 1024-1026 as optional/uncertain. But the extracted atomic operations list `PRED(branch.city = 'London' OR branch.open_year = 1025)` and `PRED(branch.city = 'London' OR branch.open_year = 2011)` as comparison_boundary targets with values [1024,1025,1026,2009,2010,2011,2012]. The program's `TextBoundarySampler` for Open_year uses range 2000..2020 with boundary_pool [2009,2010,2011,2012], so 1024-1026 can never appear, and the `OR open_year = 1025` predicate can never be satisfied by a generated row.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) confirm 1024-1026 are genuinely out of domain and remove them from the boundary targets, or (b) widen the Open_year sampler to include 1024-1026 in the boundary pool (they are integer-castable and the OR-predicate targets require them). The current spec is internally inconsistent: the semantic rule excludes them but the atomic-operation targets require them.

issues.evidence: Specification `semantic_rules_and_formulas` for branch.membership_amount says `CAST(membership_amount AS INTEGER) >= 0` and marks -32..-30 as optional/uncertain, but the atomic operations list `PRED(branch.membership_amount >= -31)` and `PRED(branch.membership_amount >= 100)` with targets [-32,-31,-30,99,100,101]. The program's `BoundaryTextSampler` uses range 0..199 with boundary_pool [99,100,101], so negative values never appear.
issues.requested_revision: Resolve the same inconsistency as Open_year: either drop the negative boundary targets or allow negative values in the sampler. If the >= 0 rule is authoritative, the -32..-30 targets should be removed from the atomic-operation list.

issues.evidence: instance.py `_spec_table_sizes` jitters sizes up by 0..3 (`v + rng.randint(0, 3)`), so membership_register_branch can be 8..11 rows. But `_fill_fk_columns` for the PK+FK Member_ID requires `len(pv) >= n` where pv is the parent member pool. With member size 10..13 and membership_register_branch size 8..11, the pool is usually large enough, but the execution feedback shows 78 skipped rows, indicating the pool check or the actual inserted parent set is inconsistent. Also `_dedup_pk` runs before FK fill and can shrink `n_final`, but `inst_pk` for the parent is recorded from `cols` after FK fill — if the parent's own FK fill or dedup changes its PK list, the child pool is stale.
issues.requested_revision: Make the parent PK list used for child FK pools exactly the list the writer inserts. Currently `inst_pk.setdefault(t, {})[cm.name] = cols[cm.name]` is set inside the per-table loop, but `_dedup_pk` and `_drop_unique_duplicates` run before FK fill and can change `n_final`; ensure the recorded `inst_pk` length matches the number of rows actually written for that table. Add an assertion that every child FK value is in the parent's final PK set before writing.

issues.evidence: writer.py disables foreign key enforcement (`pragma foreign_keys = OFF`) and only catches `sqlite3.Error` per row. With FK enforcement off, FK violations are never raised, so the row-by-row fallback never detects them and the 292 FK violations are written silently. The execution feedback's integrity check (run separately) catches them, but the generator itself does not.
issues.requested_revision: Enable `pragma foreign_keys = ON` before inserting (after copying the compact DB), or run a post-insert FK integrity check (`pragma foreign_key_check`) and raise if any violation exists. This makes the generator self-validating and prevents silent corruption.

issues.evidence: The specification's `dependencies` note for membership_register_branch.Member_ID says 'sample without replacement from parent pool; require len(parent_pool) >= n else raise clear error'. The program implements this, but the execution feedback shows 78 skipped rows, meaning the error path is not being hit (rows are skipped instead). The spec should clarify that a pool-too-small condition must abort the instance, not skip rows, and the engineer must implement that.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the spec that any constraint violation during writing must abort the instance (raise), not be silently skipped, so table sizes and FK integrity are guaranteed. The engineer should then remove the row-by-row skip fallback in writer.py or make it raise on FK/NOT NULL/PK violations.

unresolved_checks: The exact cause of the 78 skipped membership_register_branch rows is not fully determined from the feedback alone; it could be PK+FK pool exhaustion, stale parent PK list, or a NOT NULL issue on Member_ID. The engineer should reproduce with a single instance and inspect the rejected rows.

Whether the 1024-1026 and -32..-30 boundary targets are genuinely required by the query workload or are artifacts of the extraction is unresolved; the designer should confirm against the source queries.

The construction_pairs feedback shows 12 of 61 eligible pairs separated, which is low but not by itself a generation error; no action requested, but the engineer should verify after fixing FK integrity that separation improves.
